chapter.name: Network Services
chapter.description: DHCP, NAT/PAT, NTP and DNS operations on Cisco devices

questions.question: What are the four DHCP lease messages a client and server exchange?
questions.answer: DHCP Discover (client broadcast), DHCP Offer (server proposes an IP), DHCP Request (client accepts specific offer), and DHCP ACK (server confirms the lease).
questions.explanation: RENEW at 50% of lease uses unicast Request directly to the server; REBIND at 87.5% falls back to broadcast. NAK and DECLINE can also appear in troubleshooting.
acceptableAnswers: discover offer request ack
dora

questions.question: At what point of the lease does a DHCP client attempt RENEW (unicast to the server)?
questions.answer: 50% of the lease duration
questions.explanation: 50% renew, then 87.5% rebind via broadcast, then the lease expires and the client restarts Discover. Timers: T1 (renewal), T2 (rebinding).

questions.question: What is the default DHCP pool lease duration on IOS routers?
questions.answer: 1 day
questions.explanation: Default lease is 24 hours; change it with 'lease days hours minutes' inside the pool, e.g. 'lease 7'.

questions.question: Write the commands to create a DHCP pool LAN-POOL handing out 10.1.1.100-10.1.1.200 with gateway 10.1.1.1 and DNS 8.8.8.8.
questions.answer:
R1(config)# ip dhcp excluded-address 10.1.1.1 10.1.1.99
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool LAN-POOL
R1(dhcp-config)# network 10.1.1.0 /24
R1(dhcp-config)# default-router 10.1.1.1
R1(dhcp-config)# dns-server 8.8.8.8
questions.explanation: The excluded-address keeps the router, servers and static hosts out of the pool; 'domain-name' can be added too. The pool takes effect as soon as configured.
acceptableAnswers: excluded addresses then pool with network, default router, dns

questions.question: A client on VLAN 30 must get DHCP from a server on another subnet. Write the command on the VLAN 30 SVI that makes DHCP work across subnets.
questions.answer:
SW1(config)# interface Vlan30
SW1(config-if)# ip helper-address 10.9.9.5
questions.explanation: The helper receives broadcast DORA messages, changes the source to the relay agent address (giaddr), and unicasts them to the server. The server replies to the giaddr — so the relay must be reachable and the SVI for the client subnet must exist.
acceptableAnswers: ip helper address on the vlan 30 svi
dhcp relay with giaddr
hints: Which interface facing the clients carries the command?
What is the role of the giaddr field?

questions.question: Which command shows the DHCP bindings the router has handed out (IP, client ID/MAC, lease expiry)?
questions.answer: show ip dhcp binding
questions.explanation: Columns: IP address, client-ID, lease expiration, type (Automatic/Manual). An empty table usually means clients never completed DORA with this router.
acceptableAnswers: show ip dhcp binding

questions.question: Which command shows the DHCP pool statistics — number of addresses available and in use?
questions.answer: show ip dhcp pool
questions.explanation: Shows utilization per pool: total addresses, leased, exclusions. Useful to spot exhaustion.
acceptableAnswers: show ip dhcp pool

questions.question: Clients on VLAN 30 cannot get an IP; the DHCP server is on the core and sees no requests. What is the most likely misconfiguration?
questions.answer: Missing or wrongly placed 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 30 SVI (or on the wrong interface/VLAN), or the helper is configured but the SVI is down — DHCP broadcasts are never forwarded without a relay on the client-facing routed interface.
questions.explanation: Also check the giaddr returned routes back to the relay and that DHCP snooping is not dropping messages (untrusted port toward a legitimate relay).
symptoms: The DHCP server log shows zero requests
Other VLANs served by relays work fine
questions.topology: SW1 (L3) with SVI 10.1.30.1/24 for VLAN 30; DHCP server 10.9.9.5 on a different subnet
questions.showOutput:
SW1# show running-config interface Vlan30
interface Vlan30
 ip address 10.1.30.1 255.255.255.0
!
acceptableAnswers: no ip helper address on the vlan 30 svi
relay is missing
hints: Which line is absent from the running config?

questions.question: What is the difference between static NAT, dynamic NAT, and PAT?
questions.answer: Static NAT maps one inside address to one fixed outside address (bidirectional, for servers). Dynamic NAT maps a pool of public addresses to inside hosts on demand, one-to-one. PAT (overload) maps many inside addresses to a single public address, distinguishing flows by port number.
questions.explanation: Dynamic NAT fails when the pool is exhausted; PAT is the standard Internet access method. NAT terms: inside local, inside global, outside local, outside global.
acceptableAnswers: static is one to one fixed, dynamic is one to one from a pool, pat is many to one with ports
hints: Which one preserves the port number?
Which one is for inbound server access?

questions.question: In the translation table, what exactly does the inside global address represent?
choices: The public/outside-in-view address of an inside host
The private address of an inside host
The source address of the outside host
The destination the server is listening on
questions.answer: The public/outside-in-view address of an inside host
questions.explanation: Inside local = host's own private IP seen inside; inside global = the translated address seen from outside (e.g. a PAT public IP). Outside terms mirror this for remote hosts.

questions.question: Write the full configuration to PAT all inside users (10.1.0.0/16) out of public address 203.0.113.5 on Gi0/0.
questions.answer:
R1(config)# ip nat pool PUB 203.0.113.5 203.0.113.5 netmask 255.255.255.255
R1(config)# access-list 1 permit 10.1.0.0 0.0.255.255
R1(config)# ip nat inside source list 1 pool PUB overload
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0
R1(config-if)# ip nat outside
R1(config-if)# ip address dhcp
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/1
R1(config-if)# ip nat inside
questions.explanation: Alternative with single public IP: 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0 overload'. The ACL identifies inside-local networks; interfaces must be marked inside/outside correctly.
commands: ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0 overload
acceptableAnswers: acl for inside networks, overload command, inside and outside interface marks

questions.question: Publish a web server 192.168.1.10:80 as public 203.0.113.10:80 using static NAT.
questions.answer: R1(config)# ip nat inside source static tcp 192.168.1.10 80 203.0.113.10 80
questions.explanation: Follow with interface marking (inside on the LAN, outside on the WAN). For a single host: 'ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.10 203.0.113.10'.
acceptableAnswers: ip nat inside source static tcp private ip 80 public ip 80

questions.question: Which command shows active NAT translations and which shows only plain/static ones?
questions.answer: show ip nat translations (all) ; show ip nat translations static (or 'show ip nat translations verbose' for timers/internal details)
questions.explanation: PAT translations show as 'inside global -> inside local' with an outside address/port; an empty dynamic section while users browse indicates no traffic matching the ACL.
acceptableAnswers: show ip nat translations

questions.question: Users on the inside can browse the web, but only sporadically — connections stall for minutes. 'show ip nat translations' shows the pool exhausted with many entries for unused IPs. What is wrong?
questions.answer: Dynamic NAT (without overload) is running out of pool addresses; PAT/overload is missing — OR the overload keyword was left off, so each host burns a whole pool address and NAT drops new sessions when exhausted.
questions.explanation: Add 'overload' to use ports and shrink the pool need; also watch inside-local uniqueness after DHCP expiry (stale bindings).
symptoms: Intermittent total loss of outbound connectivity
Users' sessions time out without errors
show ip nat translations shows pool exhaustion
questions.topology: R1 Gi0/1 = inside (10.1.0.0/16), Gi0/0 = outside, pool PUBLIC 203.0.113.1-10
questions.showOutput:
R1# show ip nat translations
Pro Inside global      Inside local       Outside local
--- 203.0.113.3        10.1.0.5           ---
--- 203.0.113.4        10.1.0.12          ---
R1# show running-config | include nat
 ip nat inside source list 1 pool PUBLIC
acceptableAnswers: pat overload is missing so the pool exhausted
no overload keyword on the nat statement
hints: What keyword multiplies the pool capacity by ~64k?
What does each line of the show output represent?

questions.question: What is NTP, on which port does it run, and why do routers and switches need it?
questions.answer: NTP (UDP 123) synchronizes device clocks off a stratum hierarchy: stratum 0 = atomic/radio clocks, stratum 1 = directly connected to them, each hop adds one stratum. Accurate timestamps are vital for log correlation, certificates, routing protocols (e.g. EIGRP SIA timestamps), and auditing.
questions.explanation: 'ntp master' serves time locally; 'ntp server X' makes the device a client. Use 'ntp source' to bind the source interface, improving reachability through ACLs.
acceptableAnswers: udp 123, layers called stratum, keeps logs and protocols in sync
network time protocol
hints: What do we call the hierarchy levels?

questions.question: A router configured with two NTP servers picks time from which one?
choices: The server with the best stratum (lowest number), then by distance/jitter among equals
The server with the highest stratum number
questions.answer: The server with the best stratum (lowest number), then by distance/jitter among equals
questions.explanation: NTP prefers lower stratum; equal stratum compares synchronization distance. Only one server is used at a time; 'ntp peer' can also be used between hotspots.

questions.question: Write the commands to make a switch sync to NTP server 192.168.99.50 and ensure NTP packets source from Loopback0.
questions.answer:
SW1(config)# ntp server 192.168.99.50
SW1(config)# ntp source Loopback0
questions.explanation: 'show ntp status' verifies sync and stratum; 'show ntp associations' shows peers. On some platforms also 'ntp update-calendar' to persist the time into the hardware calendar.
acceptableAnswers: ntp server 192.168.99.50 and ntp source loopback 0

questions.question: Which two commands show NTP sync state (stratum, offset, ref clock) and the known NTP peers/associations?
questions.answer: show ntp status ; show ntp associations
questions.explanation: 'show ntp status' shows clock state, stratum, reference id; 'show ntp associations' lists server/peer IPs with reachability. Add 'detail' for rich debugging.
acceptableAnswers: show ntp status and show ntp associations

questions.question: How does a Cisco router use DNS and what command configures the name server?
questions.answer: Routers resolve hostnames for commands like 'ping server1' or 'telnet server1' if DNS is enabled: 'ip name-server 8.8.8.8' (up to 6 servers) and 'ip domain-lookup' (or 'ip domain-name' to append a domain suffix).
questions.explanation: Without 'ip domain-name' and lookup enabled, an unknown command is treated as a hostname attempt (the famous 'Translating ... domain server' delays from default lookup on).
acceptableAnswers: ip name-server and ip domain lookup
resolve hostnames for ping and telnet
hints: What enables the translation attempt at all?

questions.question: Typing a bogus command like 'sdgfdg' on a router with default settings produces a long delay and then 'Translating ... domain server (255.255.255.255)'. Why?
choices: The router treats it as an unknown hostname and attempts DNS resolution by default
The router is running a debug of ARP
The parser is waiting for the SNMP community
questions.answer: The router treats it as an unknown hostname and attempts DNS resolution by default
questions.explanation: Disable with 'no ip domain-lookup' or speed it up by configuring real name servers. It waits until the DNS timeout (default 3 s, 3 retries) before saying 'Translating...'.
